title: SOURCE_TARGETS validated: MODIFY COLUMN rolls back on one-shot transient reorg errors that ADD INDEX retries through

payload.validation_scope: Failpoint-instrumented local replay on the shared backfill worker plus supporting grpc-family sibling runs, then live bridge-level semantic confirmation on testbed 8220955 with commit-matched failpoint owner injection at the classifier boundary.
payload.user_symptom: A short transient connection or grpc hiccup during online MODIFY COLUMN causes the DDL to fail and roll back instead of completing after retry, while sibling ADD INDEX survives the same one-shot fault.
payload.quality_gate: Confirmed high-severity DDL availability bug: the operation is long-running, user-visible, and wasted by a single transient fault; live owner-lane red/green evidence now exists in addition to the local family extension.
payload.method_note: The decisive signal was sibling differential on the same bridge and the same one-shot fault family, plus a shared GREEN control; broader network chaos alone was weaker evidence.

provenance.source: current TiDB source plus local differential probes and live owner-lane bridge matrix

payload.description: Find a one-shot transient fault near an inner worker/result boundary, then compare sibling operations that share the same worker but have different retry bridges or terminal-state policies.
positive_signal: shared worker or shared phase boundary
one-shot foreign error or transient connection/grpc failure
per-operation retry bridge or rollback policy split
terminal state is user-visible and long-running enough to matter
required_gates: same injected fault shape lands on the same worker boundary
sibling green control exists on the same boundary
terminal state is observed after the fault, not inferred from one retry log
root cause can be compressed to a retry classifier, retry bridge, or terminalization split
negative_screens: broad infra chaos without proof of the semantic boundary
plain error-string drift without terminal-state consequence
families where all siblings fail or all siblings recover the same way
synthetic fault family with no same-altitude green control or product-feasible reachability proof

payload.contract: When a one-shot retryable fault hits an active DDL reorg worker, the observed terminal state must reflect the real recovery policy. A retry log alone is not enough evidence.
required_observers: job state immediately after the hit
sibling control on the same boundary
red_signature: job transitions to rollingback or rollback done after a one-shot transient fault
user-visible SQL returns the transient fault
outer retry log appears but the job is already doomed
green_signature: job remains running after the hit and later reaches done or synced
supporting checks such as admin check remain green
invalid_signature: fault lands outside the active reorg window
observer only sees logs and not terminal state
same injected family makes all siblings red without a natural-reachability proof

provenance.source: modify-column transient differential and add-index fast-reorg/ingest retry misclassification

setup: choose two sibling operations sharing a backfill or reorg worker
arm a one-shot transient fault at the worker result boundary
run each operation separately with the same small input
payload.workload: observe whether each sibling keeps running, rolls back, or succeeds after the same one-shot fault
controls: same table shape and row-count scale

name: Inject once then watch terminal state

steps: arm one-shot transient fault near the worker result boundary
wait for the first fault hit
continue observing after the immediate error log
record terminal state and user-visible outcome
run the sibling control with the same schedule
controls: terminal state is sampled after any outer worker retry sleep
expected_observations: RED: one-shot transient fault forces rollingback or rollback done
GREEN: one-shot transient fault is absorbed and the job reaches done or synced

state_model: shared backfill worker sends backfillResult.err to reorg consumers
inner DDL-specific handlers decide whether the error keeps the job running or flips the job to rollingback
outer job worker later persists the updated job state and may still print a generic retry log if runJobErr looks retryable
therefore retry-log presence is weaker than the terminal job state

name: Modify-column reorg must not force rollback on one-shot transient worker faults

payload.p_check: A shared backfill worker returns a one-shot transient foreign error after MODIFY COLUMN has entered active reorg.
payload.q_claim: The reorg retry bridge preserves retryability until the DDL makes its terminal-state choice, so a one-shot transient fault should not force rollback.
payload.fault: Modify-column uses isRetryableModifyColumnReorgJobError(err, jobErrCnt) -> isRetryableError(err, false). If that check fails, modify_column.go flips the job to rollingback before the outer generic worker retry loop runs.

boundary.before: backfill worker sends one transient error
boundary.after: the DDL chooses keep-running versus rollingback and eventually reaches a terminal state

source_anchors: pkg/ddl/modify_column.go:1392-1412 inner retry classifier and convert-to-rollback path
pkg/ddl/index.go:1980-1999 sibling add-index retry classifier with retryUnknown=true
pkg/ddl/job_worker.go:700-711 outer retry sleep happens after the updated job state is committed
side_effects: user-visible DDL failure for a transient fault that sibling DDLs survive
misleading retry log before eventual rollback
consumers: ALTER TABLE ... CHANGE COLUMN row-rewrite reorg

evidence.oracle: same one-shot transient worker fault must not force rollback if retryability is preserved
evidence.red_observation: All five connection-family shapes emitted a generic outer retry log first, but the persisted job had already flipped to State:rollingback and then reached State:rollback done; supporting grpc unavailable and grpc dataloss runs showed the same terminalization pattern.
key_log_lines: modify-column-transient-family-local.log:6598 modify-column invalid connection outer retry log
modify-column-transient-family-local.log:10326 modify-column connection refused outer retry log
user_visible_errors: read tcp: read: connection reset by peer

lessons.root_cause: modify_column.go marks the job rollingback on inner retryUnknown=false classification before the outer generic worker retry loop prints its sleep-and-retry log.
lessons.observer_note: Terminal state beats log text: a retry log can coexist with a doomed rollback path.
lessons.method_note: This lane became high-signal only after extending from one grpc string to a compact family of realistic transient shapes.
